label: Bible Study
prompt: Favour is _____, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
verse: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
note: The last word on the virtuous woman — charm fades, beauty passes, reverence lasts.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet _____, and all the hills shall melt.
verse: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt.
note: So much harvest the plowman catches up with the reaper — Amos ends with mountains dripping sweet wine.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And the third day there was a _____ in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:
verse: And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:
note: Jesus' first miracle happened at a wedding in Cana — the KJV calls it a marriage, and the wine was about to run out.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And now, Israel, what doth the LORD thy God _____ of thee, but to fear the LORD thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the LORD thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul,
verse: And now, Israel, what doth the LORD thy God require of thee, but to fear the LORD thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the LORD thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul,
note: The question Micah would echo centuries later: what does God actually want? Fear, walk, love, serve.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For I am _____, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
verse: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
note: The start of Paul's great list — death, life, angels, powers — that climaxes in verse 39: nothing can separate us.
